newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar steady in ranges, trade light.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar steady in ranges, trade light.

text.p: White sugar futures hovered in tight ranges as the structure of London's forward months struggled to regain its normal backwardation amid a lack of fresh fundamental news, traders said on Monday.

Market turnover stayed light throughout the session with crossed and against actuals March trades mainly concluded by commission houses comprising the bulk of the activity. The earlier weakness was partially offset by limited trade buying and a firmer New York performance. The key March raw/white premium remained steady at around $68. "It's pretty quiet but not dead," said one trader. At 1725 GMT March was unchanged at $303.00 and dominated the overall volume of 660 lots. May was just 10 cents higher at $303.90, after which further forward months reverted to their normal backwardation.
Traders said industrial users were deterred from making spot purchases by the flat spreads and were waiting for lower prices.
"You haven't really got the buyers coming in spot at the moment and pushing it up. Everyone's hunting around for a buyer in March but a lot of people are already covered," said one.

"I think there's every chance that March can go under $300, I don't see there's anything in the market to stop it unless you can get some really good buying to come out." Market sources said the raws market was unlikely to give London much of a boost this week as many raws players are thought to have their positions covered and the CSCE is closed for Thursday and Friday due to public holidays.
In physical news, Zimbabwe is thought to have bought 28,000 tonnes of raw sugar for January/February from a London-based trade house at an undisclosed price.
Paris trading was even quieter than in London. March was down 50 cents at $303.00, the same as its Lodon equivalent, and May was up 20 cents at $303.70. Matif volume totalled 265 lots.
